title: Margins & Generalization
interviewAnswer: A classification margin measures separation from the decision boundary; large-margin methods such as SVMs prefer a wider buffer while allowing controlled violations in the soft-margin case.
why: Margins connect geometry, regularization and generalization.
intuition: Two separators can classify training points correctly, but the one farther from the closest examples is less sensitive to small perturbations.
deepDive: Hard-margin SVM maximizes geometric margin; soft-margin SVM trades violations against margin size through C.
commonMistakes: Confusing weight magnitude with geometric margin.
Assuming margins solve overlapping/noisy labels automatically.
production: Margin robustness does not replace shift/feature-quality monitoring.
workedExample: For separable classes, support vectors determine the maximal-margin boundary.
